Ukrainian drones struck a major refinery deep inside Russia, military officials said Thursday, the fourth in three days in Kyiv’s monthslong campaign to choke Moscow’s vital oil sector.

Russia is one of the world’s biggest energy producers, with oil providing an economic mainstay as its army tries to push deeper into Ukraine in a slow and costly advance more than four years after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion.

The attacks have dented Russia’s refining capacity, bringing shortages at gas stations. Kyiv officials say the onslaught seeks to compel Russian President Vladimir Putin to seek a peace deal. There is no sign that strategy is working.

The refinery targeted is one of Russia's biggest facilities

Ukraine’s General Staff said that its forces struck the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining and petrochemical complex in Russia’s republic of Bashkortostan overnight, causing a fire at the facility.

Astora natural gas depot in Rehden ( Reuters )

The complex, located southeast of Moscow about 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) from Ukraine’s border, is one of Russia’s largest oil refining and petrochemical facilities, the General Staff said in a Telegram post.

The plant processes up to 74 million barrels of oil annually, producing gasoline, diesel fuel and other products, it said.

Russia’s Bashkortostan governor, Radiy Khabirov, said only that a drone attack wounded two civilians and started a fire in an industrial zone of Salavat.

Wildberries, Russia’s biggest online retailer whose giant warehouses have repeatedly been struck by Ukrainian drones, said a fire started at one of its facilities in the Salavat industrial zone after the overnight attack. The company said the facility was evacuated but that goods were not being stored there.

The attack came a day after Ukrainian anti-ship missiles and drones blitzed a major Russian naval base on the Black Sea coast.

Elsewhere, four explosive experts from Russia’s Emergency Ministry and a security guard were killed Thursday after an unspecified Ukrainian weapon exploded in Sevastopol, a port city in illegally annexed Crimea, the Russian-installed governor of Sevastopol Mikhail Razvozhayev said.

They were inspecting the site of a Ukrainian attack when “an enemy weapon detonated,” he said.

It was not possible to independently verify either side’s reports.

Russian official says another refinery's repairs could take 6 months

Meanwhile, a Russian refinery in Orsk that was hit by Ukrainian drones earlier this week has suspended operations, Orenburg region Gov. Yevgeny Solntsev said Thursday.

He said that “key infrastructure, which cannot be restored at this time” was struck, including foreign equipment, and “taking (international) sanctions into account,” the repairs could take up to six months, Solntsev said in a rare public admission in Russia of the problems Ukrainian attacks are causing.

Ukraine’s General Staff had reported striking the Orsk refinery, in Russia’s Orenburg region near the border with Kazakhstan, on Tuesday.

Russian drone hits a Ukrainian passenger train, killing 2

Russia has responded by hammering Ukraine with ballistic missiles, jet-powered drones and glide bombs, all of which are powerful and hard to intercept. The strikes have killed more than 16,000 civilians since the war began, according to the United Nations.

Russian attacks featuring 133 long-range strike drones killed at least four people and wounded eight others across Ukraine overnight from Wednesday to Thursday, officials said.

A jet-powered Shahed drone struck a passenger train in the southern Odesa region, killing the engineer and his assistant, Ukraine’s state railway company, Ukrzaliznytsia, said Thursday.

A Russian drone killed two men on Wednesday evening in the southern city of Kherson, regional military administration chief Oleksandr Prokudin said.

Ukraine makes little headway on obtaining Patriot missiles

Ukraine desperately wants more U.S.-made Patriot interceptor missiles that can counter Russia's ballistic missiles, but stocks of the air defense system reportedly are low because of the Iran war.

Ukraine so far this year has two and a half times fewer Patriot interceptors than in 2025, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, saying he makes calls every day to try and source some more.

He said in an interview with CNN broadcast Wednesday evening, parts of which he posted on social media, that he is asking the United States to sell 5% of the interceptor missiles they have in stock to help Ukraine make it through next winter, when Russia’s strikes focus on the power grid.

He has so far obtained just 1%, he said.

In the first half of this year, European countries paid U.S. defense companies at least 3 billion euros ($3.5 billion) for military equipment they sent to Ukraine, according to a report Thursday by Germany’s Kiel Institute, which tracks assistance to Kyiv.

The Trump administration won’t provide its own aid to Ukraine but is allowing other countries to buy U.S. equipment that is sent on.

Military aid provided to Ukraine in the first half of 2026 was close to last year’s level, the Kiel Institute said, but financial and humanitarian aid was 41% lower than in 2025.

Nigel Farage beat trash-can wearing comic candidate Count Binface on Friday, regaining a seat in Parliament he quit a month ago to trigger the widely mocked special election.

Farage received 22,239 votes and Binface, who finished in second, won nearly 9,500 votes. The election, held on the hottest day of the year so far, had turnout of 44%.

Farage, leader of the anti-immigration Reform UK party who some see as a possible next prime minister, abruptly quit his seat in July amid an investigation into whether he failed to report a 5 million pound ($6.7 million) gift from a crypto billionaire overseas.

He said he would run for the open seat to prove he had voters’ support.

Binface, a serial candidate who has challenged prime ministers past and present, became the default challenger in a field of 34 candidates after the major parties boycotted the campaign as a political stunt by Farage.

Farage declared victory in the early morning and did not attend the official declaration where he would have had to stand alongside the other candidates, many of them running joke campaigns.

Binface ran on a wacky platform that included a vow to “cut your taxes, and raise everyone else’s,” build one affordable home and nationalize singer Adele.

The victory by Farage showed his strong support in the Clacton area on the east coast of England but it doesn’t ensure he’ll be able to keep the seat.

An investigation by a parliamentary watchdog that was suspended when he stepped down is likely to resume. It could lead to Farage being forced out and result in yet another election.

Online buyer searches for homes for sale featuring air conditioning have more than doubled during the late spring and summer months compared to last year.

Property portal Rightmove recorded a 104% increase in user searches across its website between May 1 and July 31, compared with the identical period from a year earlier.

The UK experienced its hottest day of the year so far on Thursday as temperatures soared to 38.1C in Kew Gardens.

Thursday also set a new record for the number of days above 36C in a single year.

Meanwhile, amber warnings for “extreme heat” came into force across parts of England, and a yellow weather warning for thunderstorms is in place for Northern Ireland.

Last week, Citizens Advice found that one in one in six Britons are taking "drastic action" to cope with heatwaves, including sleeping in kitchens, missing work, or booking hotels.

open image in gallery An estate agent has noted an important change in buyer behaviour ( Alamy/PA )

The charity warns millions across the UK are "trapped in homes they can’t cool", with almost half (44%) feeling powerless to prevent their houses overheating.

The study attributes this struggle to poorly designed homes, which act as "heat traps", and the high cost of cooling equipment such as air conditioning, leaving people helpless.

Colleen Babcock, a property expert at Rightmove, said: “This summer’s heatwaves appear to be influencing how people think about their homes.”

Mark Wiggin, director of Mark Wiggin Estate Agents, said: “Energy efficiency and a home’s ability to stay comfortable throughout the year have become much more important considerations when people are deciding where to live.”

James Waight, head of sales at John D Wood & Co said: “We are seeing buyers pay closer attention to air conditioning, ventilation and how well a home retains a comfortable temperature during warmer months.”

open image in gallery Comfort and liveability are increasingly being considered alongside traditional factors such as location, space and price, an estate agent said ( Getty Images )

Ian Harris, president of NAEA (National Association of Estate Agents) Propertymark said: “Whilst air conditioning is clearly becoming a more visible feature on buyers’ wish lists, agents are seeing a broader shift in what people want from a home: comfort and liveability are increasingly being considered alongside traditional factors such as location, space and price.

“What is particularly interesting is that buyers are becoming more alert to how a property will perform in different conditions, rather than simply looking at individual features.

“Agents are increasingly fielding questions about ventilation, natural shade, glazing, orientation and energy costs, with buyers wanting to understand what living in a property will actually feel like throughout the year.

“This is an important change in buyer behaviour. As hotter summers become more familiar, the ability of a home to remain comfortable in warm weather is likely to become a more established consideration during viewings and valuations, rather than something buyers only think about once they have moved in.”

Conditions across the UK housing market remained subdued during July, with buyer demand and agreed sales displaying few indications of a significant recovery, according to surveyors.

A net balance of 28% of property professionals surveyed reported a decline in new buyer inquiries in July, a figure that was unchanged from June, the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (Rics) said.

Despite remaining negative, the figure shows an improvement from a recent low net balance of 41% of professionals in March, which Rics noted indicates that the overall pace of deteriorating demand has eased.

Manchester is one of my favourite UK cities to visit. It is just an hour away from where I live in the Lake District, which makes it perfect for a quick shopping and foodie trip when I want a change of scene.

It’s a city with a big personality, shaped by its industrial past, music history – with its famous links to the punk scene and Northern Soul – football culture, and an ever-evolving food scene. There’s so much to do, whether you want independent shops, galleries, markets or rooftop drink.

For wheelchair users, though, a city break is never just about what there is to see. You need to be able to find reliable access information before you travel, and for it to hold up beyond the obvious tourist spots.

So how does Manchester stack up to the likes of London, Glasgow or Edinburgh as an accessible destination?



Getting around

open image in gallery Metrolink stops in Manchester are step-free with level boarding ( Marketing Manchester )

Manchester Piccadilly has direct rail connections to London, Birmingham, Liverpool, Leeds, Sheffield, Glasgow and Edinburgh. Services into the city offer wheelchair spaces, accessible toilets and the option to book boarding assistance through Passenger Assist, although I would always recommend checking your route and train operator in advance.

Manchester Piccadilly has step-free access throughout, with lifts connecting platforms and the main concourse. When you roll out of the station, you are already in the city, without needing to navigate complicated exits or secondary routes.

From there, several central neighbourhoods sit close together. The Northern Quarter, Spinningfields and Deansgate can all be combined in one trip. Distances are manageable enough that you can adjust your route as you go, rather than committing to a fixed plan.

For longer distances, the Metrolink tram system is one of my favourite ways to get around independently. Platforms are step-free with level boarding and only a minimal gap, so getting on and off does not require precision or assistance. There are clear, designated spaces for wheelchair users on board.

Accessible taxis, including black cabs, are easy to hail across the city centre if you want a sure-fire option.

What to see and do

Northern Quarter

open image in gallery Many of the Northern Quarter's independent shops, cafes and bars are clustered around Oldham Street ( Marketing Manchester )

The Northern Quarter sits between Piccadilly Gardens, Shudehill and Ancoats, with many of its independent shops, cafes and bars clustered around Oldham Street, Tib Street and Thomas Street. It is one of Manchester’s most creative neighbourhoods, known for vintage fashion, record shops, street art and small businesses you won’t find on the average high street.

Manchester Craft and Design Centre on Oak Street is one of the more interesting shopping stops. Set inside a former Victorian fish market, it brings together independent makers selling jewellery, prints, and homewares. Both entrances are step-free, with an accessible toilet, workshops and several studios on the ground floor. There is no lift to the first floor, although staff can bring products downstairs if something catches your eye from one of the upstairs studios.

From an accessibility point of view, the pavements in the Northern Quarter are mostly level and wide enough to move through comfortably, though some streets can feel busy at peak times. It’s a good area to explore slowly, with plenty of places to stop for coffee, and it’s easy to alter your plans plans if the weather turns.

Spinningfields

Spinningfields, the city’s financial centre, is the place to go to see the glossier side of Manchester. This part of the city is known for its restaurants, cocktail bars, outdoor terraces and after-work buzz. It’s a good option for dinner, drinks or a livelier end to the day, with great venues close together.

Access is generally straightforward, because many of the restaurants and bars are newer, with level entrances from the street, wider doorways and outdoor seating areas. It’s easy to browse options, rather than committing to a venue before you know whether you can actually get inside comfortably.

Afflecks

Indoor market, Afflecks, is on Church Street in the heart of the Northern Quarter, a short distance from Market Street and Manchester Arndale. Spread across several floors, it’s packed with small independent businesses.

Part of the fun comes from never quite knowing what you’ll find. The Manchester Shop on the ground floor sells locally inspired clothing, gifts and the city’s famous bee merchandise, while Mad for Art specialises in vintage prints and retro s. Panino 23 on the first floor is a great lunch stop, serving Italian sandwiches and handmade desserts.

open image in gallery Afflecks Manchester ( Carrie-Ann Lightly )

Access is better than you might expect from an older, multi-level building. There is step-free access via a portable ramp, a lift to all floors and an accessible toilet on level one. Some individual units are compact, so you may need to pick your route carefully. The entrance ramp is steep, but staff are incredibly helpful.

Manchester Arndale

Manchester Arndale sits at the heart of the city centre, with entrances from Market Street, High Street and Corporation Street. It is the practical stop on a shopping day, with high street favourites from Apple to Lego and Sephora, alongside more niche fashion, beauty, tech and homeware stores.

The range makes it useful when you want choice, shelter and a predictable layout. Halle Place on the lower level also has several places to eat, including Archie’s, a colourful Manchester-born burger and shake restaurant, and Barburrito, where burrittos can be customised with your choice of fillings.

Accessibility is straightforward throughout, with step-free routes, wide walkways and enough space to move at your own pace. There are accessible toilets within the centre, as well as a Changing Places toilet, which adds extra reassurance if you need more space, support or equipment during a longer visit.

Manchester Art Gallery

Manchester Art Gallery is free to visit and has collections spanning six centuries of fine and contemporary art, as well as sculptures and decorative art. It’s particularly known for its Victorian and pre-Raphaelite paintings. You can wander through the permanent collection, spend time in a temporary exhibition, or simply use it as a quieter place to pause between exploring busier parts of the city. Currently on (until February 2028), Worn: The Life Within Clothes, explores the stories of clothing through a slow fashion lens.

Accessibility is refreshingly easy here, with level-entry, generous circulation space and seating throughout. The gallery also offers accessible toilets on the ground and first floors.

open image in gallery Manchester Art Gallery has collections spanning six centuries ( Marketing Manchester )

For blind and partially sighted visitors, some tours and events include audio description, while BSL tours and interpreters are available for some events. Find out more about the programme before you visit at manchesterartgallery.org



Where to eat and drink

Freight Island

Freight Island is one of Manchester's most distinctive food and drink destinations, bringing together independent kitchens, bars and entertainment in a huge former railway depot next to Piccadilly Station. Whether you fancy pizza, tacos, burgers, Asian street food or cocktails, there is plenty of choice, making it a good option if everyone in your group wants something different.

The scale of the venue also works well from an accessibility point of view. There is step-free access throughout, wide routes between seating areas, accessible toilets and plenty of space to move around without feeling squeezed between tables.

The Foundry Project

The Foundry Project is a relaxed Northern Quarter spot that works well for anything from brunch to an early evening meal. The menu covers crowd-pleasing comfort food, including burgers, pizzas, small plates and cocktails, so is ideal for a casual meal.

Access-wise, it feels spacious and easy to settle into, with comfortable movement between tables, accessible toilets, and plenty of allergy-friendly food options on the menu.

Runyon’s Bar and Restaurant, voco Manchester

Runyon’s Bar and Restaurant sits on the ground floor of voco Manchester hotel, close to Manchester Piccadilly, Oxford Road and the city centre. It’s smart but relaxed, and serves breakfast, lunch, dinner or cocktails. The menu combines British comfort food, including fish and chips and burgers, with internationally inspired dishes such as honey gochujang pork belly and Keralan cauliflower curry. It feels polished without being too formal.

Level access from the spacious reception takes you through to the bar and restaurant, and accessible public toilets are available.

Where to stay

open image in gallery Carrie-Ann at The Reach at Piccadilly, Manchester ( Carrie-Ann Lightly )

voco Manchester

voco Manchester shows what can happen when accessibility is considered as part of the design, rather than an afterthought. Formerly Hotel Brooklyn, the hotel retains its distinctive New York-inspired style, with dark wood features, rich velvet furnishings, brass details and monochrome bathrooms creating a boutique feel.

The hotel has 18 adapted bedrooms, including nine wheelchair accessible rooms and nine ambulant accessible rooms. Two of the wheelchair accessible rooms have ceiling track hoists, which are still rare in UK hotels and can make a huge difference for guests who need them.

Bathrooms are level access wet rooms that feel luxurious rather than clinical, with fittings positioned to make the space practical to use. The whole experience removes some of the usual negotiation that comes with accessible hotel stays.

Price: From £70

The Reach at Piccadilly, Manchester

The Reach at Piccadilly is a newer addition to Manchester's hotel scene, sitting just a few minutes from Piccadilly Station and within easy rolling distance of the Northern Quarter. Its central location makes it a great base if you want to explore without relying on taxis or public transport.

The design reflects the hotel’s canal-side setting and Manchester’s industrial heritage – with natural materials, warm finishes and subtle narrowboat-inspired details creating a stylish sense of place.

The hotel offers accessible bedrooms with step-free access and spacious layouts, as well as roll-in showers and practical bathroom fittings. Public areas are easy to navigate, with lifts serving all floors and level access throughout.

Price: From £110

So is Manchester accessible?

Not perfectly so, but it stands out among many of the UK cities I have visited. There are step-free routes, accessible transport options, spacious culture stops, practical shopping areas and enough cafes, bars and restaurants close together that one inaccessible doorway does not have to derail the whole day.

Manchester still has its older, inaccessible buildings, busy streets and occasional access compromises, but it also gives you options. For wheelchair users, that can be the difference between a trip that feels managed and one that is genuinely enjoyable.

News.title: ‘More pain’ to come after economic slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter of the year, official figures show, under pressure from the Iran war.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc between April and June, down from 0.6pc in the first three months of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The figures underline the challenge that the conflict poses for Andy Burnham, who has pledged to deliver “growth in every postcode”.

The Prime Minister has already been warned that the economy will slow further next year if Donald Trump continues his war in the Middle East.

Treasury officials have predicted UK growth of just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked for the rest of this year.

That is far lower than the 1.6pc predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March, based on assumptions made before the start of the war. Here is what you need to know.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

Team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

CELTA VIGO’s opening-day LaLiga clash with Osasuna has been postponed due to FUNGUS ravaging the pitch.

Celta ground staff had been working their fingers to the bone trying to rectify the outbreak that had ruined the playing surface.

Celta, Osasuna and the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) all agreed to postpone the match following a LaLiga inspection.

Celta said: “LaLiga agreed this morning, in coordination with the clubs and the RFEF, to postpone or find that it had to face Celta and CA Osasuna this Sunday in Abanca Balaídos due to an illness that affected the stadium’s grass, which at this time is not suitable for soccer practice.

Sports.title: West Ham bans much mocked half-and-half scarves from stadium for new season as fans are warned they will be confiscated
Sports.content:
WEST Ham bosses have banned much mocked half-and-half scarves for good.

The divisive neckwear — bearing the names of both home and away teams — are sold outside grounds across the country and are popular with tourists.

But die-hard fans despise them, and they are sometimes outlawed for one-off games against rivals as displaying away colours at the home end poses safety risks.



The Hammers, newly relegated to the Championship, have posted warning signs at their City of ­London Stadium.



They state: “West Ham United would like to remind supporters that half-and-half scarves and any items displaying the colours or crests of both clubs are permanently banned inside London Stadium.

“This policy applies at all fixtures.

“Supporters arriving with half-and-half scarves purchased from unofficial sellers will be required to hand them over to security staff at the security checkpoints and these scarves will not be returned.



“Fans wishing to purchase a scarf for the game are encouraged to visit the official West Ham United Stadium Store where a full range of official merchandise is available ahead of kick-off.”

The rule was brought in for the Hammers’ 3-1 League Cup win over Portsmouth last weekend.

The move divided fans. West Ham nut John Hayes told The Sun: “The scarves are for the tourists who take away from the match atmosphere created by die-hard fans, who are often priced out of attending by the rubberneckers.

“Having a rival club’s crest on view in the home end sparks all sorts of problems.



“These scarves deserve going into the bin — with hydration breaks.”

But Arsenal fan Frank DuPont hit back: “Football is meant to be for everyone.

Tourists spend the most in the club shops, and picking up a half-and-half scarf from a street vendor is not going to damage the match experience for fussy season ticket holders.”

Previous West Ham games where the scarves have been banned include last season’s home match against Tottenham Hotspur.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Efsixteen returns in hot Newbury race
Sports.content:
We have an interesting day's racing on Friday with Flat action from Newbury and Yarmouth, live on Sky Sports Racing...

5.23 Newbury - Efsixteen heads Listed race field

Compelling debut winner Efsixteen steps up in class in the Listed St Hugh's Stakes.

Victorious Forever and George Scott unleashed the 350,000gns Tattersalls Craven Breeze-Up purchase at Newmarket on Guineas weekend where she showed plenty of ability to beat subsequent Listed winners Crownbreaker and Havana Sprite. Her handler took the patient approach in skipping Royal Ascot, and if there have been no major issues since, she could be the one to beat.

The Charlie Appleby-trained Acting Lady won a maiden at the Newmarket July meeting which is working out well, and she clashes with Sexy Chick again who got the better of her on debut before she also went on to get off the mark in good style.

Fast Track poses a formidable threat, having improved since a creditable run in the Queen Mary, when bolting up at Beverley and finishing a good second to the well-thought-of Wild Blossom at Glorious Goodwood.

Blue Flight and Cosmic Mystery shaped better than their finishing positions last time out, with a sharp five furlongs looking sure to suit.

Acclamation Star ran on well in a hot renewal of the Duchess Of Cambridge Stakes, and backed that up when a close second as she was shouldering a heavy weight in a nice nursery at Newmarket. She should be very competitive, and Angels Lane cannot be discounted after an encouraging second over course and distance in the Super Sprint last month.

4.45 Newbury - Sorrengail faces eye-catching Evenfall

Sorrengail clashes with impressive debut winner Evenfall in the Betvictor Watch Weekend Winners EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes.

Sorrengail backed up an eye-catching debut effort with another smart performance to score at Ascot, beating next-time-out winner Speed of Sound in the process. With Rockfel and Cheveley Park entries, she is a filly with a nice future, and should be going well here.

Evenfall is one of two in the field that puts her unbeaten credentials on the line, and was arguably the most impressive debutant when scoring by nearly two lengths over Musselburgh novice winner Minster Man. If she can back up that display, she could be tough for Sorrengail to overcome.

Ferrystream is also unbeaten having won well on debut at Windsor last month, with Spirit Of Lyra looking to back up her impressive win at Lingfield where she took a sizeable step forward after an average debut.

Coat Of Red is a half-sister to high-class Group Two winner Chindit and showed that quality on her second start when winning easily, with further improvement on the cards.

2.03 Yarmouth - Matins returns for Haggas

Promising prospect Matins returns in the Download The Quinnbet App "Confined" Novice Stakes.

Matins looked very professional on debut when showing an abundance of ability to score in taking fashion. He is half-brother to the smart Group Two winner and Group One-placed Sacred, so this William Haggas-trained three-year-old could yet grow into an even better prospect, particularly when stepping up in trip.

His opposition comes in the form of the Ilka Gansera-Leveque-trained Emperor Aurelius, who will have to exceed expectations to give the stable their first winner of the year.

Best of the rest

3.35 Newbury - 500,000gns Frankel colt Quicken Away debuts for Andrew Balding.

4.10 Newbury - Al Samsama attempts to defy a penalty when opposing Ascot eye-catcher Sweetwonderfulyou.

5.58 Newbury - Trappy handicap with a few interesting runners.

2.38 Yarmouth - Godolphin's 1m gns yearling Rock Montreal debuts.

3.13 Yarmouth - Divot bids for a hat-trick.

3.03 Clairefontaine - Zulu Chant headlines Listed affair.

Sports.title: Super League leaders Leeds beaten by Leigh after late drama
Sports.content:
Innes Senior scored twice as Leigh Leopards inflicted a first home defeat of the season on Betfred Super League leaders Leeds Rhinos by winning 20-16 at Headingley.

Wing Senior went over twice in the first half after team-mate Josh Charnley's effort had cancelled out Ryan Hall's opener for Leeds, for whom Brodie Croft also touched down before the break.

In balmy, energy-sapping conditions after the hottest day in the UK this year, Leigh scored a fourth try through centre Umyla Hanley early in the second period and then withstood heavy pressure to seal a deserved win.

Ryan Hall thought his late effort for Leeds had tied the scores, but his foot was clearly in touch as he grounded the ball in the corner and Leigh clung on.

Hall touched down in the corner for the opening try in the second minute after taking Jake Connor's quick pass following a high kick, but Leigh's response was immediate as Charnley raced over following Hanley's line break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leigh Leopards head coach Adrian Lam reflects on their Super League win at Leeds Rhinos.

Connor's penalty in front of the posts for a shoulder barge on Kallum Watkins edged Leeds 8-6 ahead, but Leigh piled on the pressure midway through the first half and got their reward.

Senior powered over near the touchline and despite Leeds full-back Lachlan Miller's brilliant tackle, the video referee ruled the Leigh winger had dotted down before going out of bounds to put his side 10-8 up.

Leeds came roaring back when Croft burst through a gap under the posts for a converted score to nudge them 14-10 in front.

Rhinos centre Jack Bird went off for a head injury assessment following a clattering tackle and was replaced by teenager Zak Lloyd, whose terrific last-ditch tackle halted Charnley soon after.

But quick hands saw Leigh spin the ball left for Senior to go over on the outside to level the scores at 14-14 at half-time after Cook had missed his second conversion attempt.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur reflects on their Super League defeat to Leigh Leopards.

Connor landed his second penalty to give Leeds a two-point advantage soon after the restart following Cook's off-the-ball block on Ash Handley.

Leigh responded again though, carving open the Rhinos' defence via another slick handling move that sent Hanley over for the visitors' fourth try of the match, with Cook adding the extras to put them 20-16 in front.

The visitors were reduced to 12 men when second row Andy Badrock was sin-binned for his dangerous tackle on Harry Newman with 17 minutes to go.

Leeds threatened to make their extra man count, but they lacked composure and failed to execute in the face of some desperate, scrambling defending from Leigh.

Image: Umyla Hanley (R) celebrates scoring Leigh's final try

With three minutes remaining, Leeds thought they had drawn level when Handley sent Hall over in the corner following Connor's high kick.

But the video referee revealed the winger's foot was in touch as he grounded the ball and Leigh held firm before celebrating an impressive win.

Leeds' defeat gives Wigan Warriors the chance to move level with them at the top of the table on 36 points when they visit struggling Bradford Bulls on Sunday.

The victory kept Leigh on course for the playoffs as they tightened their grip on sixth by moving six points clear of St Helens, who can claim a maximum of 10 points from their five remaining games.

Warrington beat York to go third

Warrington Wolves beat York Knights 30-10 at the Halliwell Jones Stadium to move back up to third.

York had taken an early lead after Warrington failed to deal with a high kick and Paul McShane went over in the corner.

The Wolves - looking to edge ahead above play-off rivals Wakefield - then got themselves in front after nine minutes when Josh Thewlis darted through to slide in under the posts and Ewan Irwin added the extras.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Warrington Wolves and York Knights.

The Knights, though, soon responded again when Cody Hunter's low kick was not gathered by the Warrington backline and Jon Bennison latched onto the loose ball in the right corner.

Sam Stone, returning to the side following a three-month injury lay-off, chased George Williams' kick on the left wing and dived full length to just touch the ball down as he slid off into the advertising boards, before 18-year-old Irwin scored a fine individual try, stepping inside to burst clear, and his penalty then put Warrington 18-10 ahead at half-time.

York were punished for giving away penalties early in the second half when hooker Danny Walker took the ball a couple of yards out to spin under the posts.

Image: Ewan Irwin (R) celebrates scoring one of Warrington's five tries

Irwin then picked up a loose ball to sprint clear and run in a 60-yard try - but his celebrations were cut short after a lengthy video review decided James Bentley had knocked Denive Balmforth's arm, which caused him to fumble possession.

After a breakaway from Hunter, which looked set for a York try, was called back for what looked a tight offside call, Warrington made sure when Aaron Lindop went over in the corner after Albert Hopoate had tapped back a high kick and Irwin then slotted over a late penalty.

Hull KR maintained their push for a home play-off with a comfortable 28-10 victory over Catalans Dragons.

The home side led 22-6 after a dominant first half that saw Jack Broadbent touch down twice as Jez Litten and Joe Burgess also scored.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Hull KR and Catalans Dragons.

Tyrone May all but sealed victory with the first score of the second half after 62 minutes, before Tommy Makinson hit back with a late consolation try for Catalans.

The victory kept Hull ahead of Leigh in fifth on points difference, and moved them within just two points of Warrington and Wakefield in third and fourth.

Sports.title: Gay out for duck as Pakistan impress against County Select XI
Sports.content:
England opening batter Emilio Gay was out for a duck as Pakistan made a strong start to their tour against a Professional County Club Select XI.

Concerns over Gay's fitness for England's first Test against Pakistan, which starts on August 19, were allayed by the left-hander's inclusion for the game at Beckenham, but he made the worst possible start.

The 27-year-old, who had suffered a shoulder issue playing for Durham last week, was caught off the bowling of Mohammad Abbas by Salan Agha at second slip, having failed to score from his 12 balls faced.

PCCSXI would go on to be bowled out for 305, with captain Tom Haines, Caleb Falconer and Saif Zaib contributing half-centuries before Matthew Fisher, who is in England's 16-player squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan, made a crucial unbeaten 62 batting at 10.

James Rew, who made his England Test debut against New Zealand in June, was also dismissed cheaply as he fell for just four to Abbas.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew that was previously imposed on his team.

Abbas (3-37) and Mohammad Ali (3-23) were the pick of the Pakistan bowlers, while Khurram Shahzad (2-55) also chipped with a couple of wickets despite being more expensive.

There was also a wicket apiece for Aamer Jamal (1-32) and Ali Usman (1-38).

Pakistan then put themselves in a strong position in the three-day contest by reaching 44-0 at the close, with Azan Awais (15*) and Imam-ul-Haq (26*) seeing out the final 13 overs of the day.

Fisher was economical as he went for just seven runs from his four overs, while the other PCCSXI player who is in England's Test squad, spinner Shoaib Bashir, bowled two overs at the end of the day.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England selector Marcus North reflects on the latest decisions around the Test side and explains the involvement of Stephen Fleming.

Both sides are fielding more than XI players in the match, with Pakistan attempting to give as many of their touring squad as possible match practice ahead of Tests at Headingley, Lord's and Edgbaston.

England will be led captained by Joe Root following his reappointment as captain after Ben Stokes retired from international cricket during the final Test of the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand in June.

England also have a new head coach in Stephen Fleming, who has replaced Brendon McCullum but is not taking charge of the side during the Pakistan series, for which Marcus Trescothick will be in interim charge.

Sports.title: McIlroy makes woeful start to FedExCup Playoffs as Spieth shares lead
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy made a woeful start to the FedExCup Playoffs as he shot four-over par opening round at the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis.

Playing for the first time since finishing tied for 40th at The Open at Royal Birkdale almost a full month ago, McIlroy was level par going into the final three holes before a disastrous streak left him towards the rear of the field.

Dropped shots at 16 and 17 were followed by a double bogey at TPC Southwind's final hole, which came after McIlroy found the water with his tee shot to the closing par four.

The 74 left McIlroy nine shots adrift of the first-round leaders, with Jordan Spieth among a group of five Americans to finish on five-under par.

Spieth, who started the week outside of the top 50 players in the FedExCup standings that will go through next week's BMW Championship, is joined in the lead by Michael Thorbjornsen, Kurt Kitayama, Jake Knapp and Michael Kim.

Spieth said: "I just tried to come into this week and just be as patient, non-reactive as possible, dumb it down to try to win the golf tournament and not worry about anything else."

England's Tommy Fleetwood, who was paired with Spieth, was a shot off the lead after opening up with a 66 that included a delightful chip in for eagle at the par-five third hole.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tommy Fleetwood produced this eagle on third hole at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.

Fleetwood said: "I feel good. I didn't really play very good in the practice days. Game's not really been that great. I've been showing a lot, like some good and some really not so good.

"Hit it great off the tee today. Still my iron play was iffy, but I did a good job of managing it for the most part. Still hit some really good shots, and you can never underestimate how good - I think shooting under par on this golf course is very good."

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler, who played alongside McIlroy in the marquee group for the opening two rounds, put himself in a solid position by delivering a 68.

Scheffler said: "I felt like I hit a lot of quality shots with my irons.I did a good job of being patient and not trying to force it too much.

"I feel like I was right on the edge of having a good day, kind of all day is how I would describe it. So, I felt like patience-wise, I did a pretty good job."

Fleetwood had European company towards the top of the leaderboard, with Ludvig Aberg, Viktor Hovland and Sepp Straka joining Scheffler on two-under.

Shane Lowry posted a solid one-under round to start the week, while Matt Fitzpatrick was left frustrated by a closing double bogey that dropped him back to level par.

McIlroy could at least take consolation from not having the worst round of the day, which belonged to Scotland's Robert MacIntyre, who shot a 12-over par 82.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Sky Sports Golf Podcast, Jamie Weir and Brad Faxon debate whether Rory McIlroy's extended break since The Open will help him win a record-extending fourth FedExCup title.

Justin Rose also made a slow start as he finished on three-over, with fellow Englishmen Aaron Rai and Harry Hall faring little better as they finished two over.

Memphis is hosting the first of three FedExCup Playoffs events, with only the top 50 in the overall season standings at the end of Sunday's final round progressing to the BMW Championship, and then the top 30 qualifying for the season-ending Tour Championship.

McIlroy's position of 12th out of the 70-player field means there is no concern about his progress to the BMW Championship, while the fact the events have no cut gives him plenty of time to climb the leaderboard over the weekend.

How do the FedExCup Playoffs work?

All season long, players have earned points based on how they have performed in PGA Tour events, with extra points available for the signature events and majors.

Only the top 70 in the standings have reached the FedEx St Jude Championship (August 13-16), with just the top 50 then progressing to the BMW Championship (August 20-23) and then only the top 30 making it to the finale, The Tour Championship (August 27-30).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brooks Koepka was extremely disappointed after failing to make the FedExCup playoffs.

Winners of the first two play-off events earn 750 points apiece - the same as The Players and the majors - before the points reset to zero ahead of the Tour Championship.

In the closing event, all players begin at even par, with the starting-strokes model based on FedExCup placings at that point axed in 2025.

The winner of the Tour Championship becomes FedExCup champion for 2026, earning $10m (£7.4m) and a five-year PGA Tour exemption.

Live coverage of the first event of the PGA Tour's FedExCup Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship, continues at 5pm on Friday. Watch live on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event or stream with no contract.

Sports.title: Leicester City up for sale for more than £200m
Sports.content:
Thai owners King Power are seeking to sell Leicester City for more than £200m.

The former Premier League champions engaged with Citibank to sound out potential buyers, it was reported last month.

Sky Sports News has now seen a sales pitch brochure produced by the investment bank, detailing the investment opportunity and the infrastructure which is included for sale at the club.

The dossier lists as up for sale: the men's and women's teams, King Power Stadium, both the women's and the men's training facilities, and OH Leuven, Leicester's sister club in Belgium.

The project is titled "Project Lineup" and values the physical assets at £224m with no specific sum placed on the sale of King Power's football teams.

In 2023, the club purchased the land around the King Power stadium for redevelopment, with plans to expand the capacity to 40,000, build a new hotel and entertainment complex.

Citigroup forecast the club's revenue during the 2026 financial year to be £97m.

However, the bank do not mention the club's two relegations between 2023 and 2025 and the financial losses that caused.

Image: Leicester City won the Premier League 10 years ago but are now in League One

King Power, run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family, bought Leicester for £35m from Milan Mandaric in 2010.

In recent years, King Power have converted a lot of debt into equity, to the tune of almost £300m. That has meant, apart from some small maintenance loans, the club is largely debt-free.

Sky Sports News has been told King Power have no urgency to sell, and they will continue to fund the club to the fullest until such time as a new, credible buyer steps forward. They have backed head coach Russell Martin this summer, with nine new signings.

The document states that Leicester is the sixth most successful team in English football since 2000, making this a "rare opportunity" to buy a club with a record of "winning promotions to higher divisions".

Image: Leicester City famously won the Premier League in 2015/16

As well as their surprise Premier League win in 2016, Leicester also won the FA Cup and Community Shield in 2021.

These successes are all included in the sales pitch, but their current position in League One is not referenced.

The document also cites Ben Chilwell, Harvey Barnes and Kieran Dewsbury-Hall as profitable recent transfers, with Gary Lineker and Emile Heskey listed at notable former players.

Sky Sports News contacted Leicester City for comment but they have declined to do so.

Analysis: 'Finding the right purchaser could take years'

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett:

"On the face of it, it seems bizarre that King Power would look to sell Leicester City at a time when the club is at its lowest ebb, and at one of its lowest market values, with the team in League One after three relegations in four seasons.

"But in truth Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha has been seeking new investment for several years - all that is new here is the glossy brochure which advertises the club for sale, accentuating its assets. It is now being actively marketed for sale by financial specialists.

Image: Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha holding the FA Cup

"That brochure - unusual as it is - is concrete evidence of a looming end of an era. King Power want out - having delivered unprecedented success in the form of the most unlikely of Premier League titles, an FA Cup, Champions League football and a Community Shield.

"For some Leicester fans, all that success has been tarnished by recent failures, and there have been protests against the ownership, and the director of football, Jon Rudkin. Serious mistakes have been made, for sure, in the management of the club in recent years, which has seen Leicester crash into League One, after boasting to be the club which came closest to breaking the "Big Six" Premier League monopoly over the last decade.

"But those dissenting Leicester fans should be careful what they wish for. On the open market, the football club is a very attractive prospect - almost entirely debt-free (thanks to the generosity of King Power in turning almost all of their £300m debt into equity in recent years) and with fully owned assets that are the envy of much bigger clubs in the Premier League. Their Seagrave training ground is a better facility than all but a handful of others in Europe.

"However, despite all their recent success, Leicester's fan-base is not as sizeable as many of the big clubs in the Championship, and having dropped into the third tier, even promotion at the first attempt would mean they didn't have the benefit of parachute payments in the second tier. All of those facts will be taken into account by would-be buyers.

"So don't expect a quick sale of the club. It could take years to find the right purchaser. The good news for Foxes fans is that King Power will not relinquish their responsibility as custodians, just because they have made the decision to sell. Nine new signings this summer is evidence of their determination to still support the football club. And the goodwill that the Thai business leaders still have for Leicester will almost certainly mean that they won't sell to the highest bidder, just to make a quick buck.

"Khun "Top" knows his legacy is at stake, and in memory of his late father, who died tragically in a helicopter crash in the stadium car park, he will no doubt want to sell the club to a new owner who can take the club forward, and once again make it a success."

Sports.title: Draper beaten in Cincinnati first round after blowing second-set lead
Sports.content:
Jack Draper lost 6-3 7-5 to Martin Landaluce in the first round of the Cincinnati Open after blowing six set-point chances to level the match.

Little more than a week on from a first-round defeat in Montreal on his return from injury, Draper was once more unable to maintain a consistent level as he succumbed to the Spaniard.

After being broken in the first game of the match on his way to losing the first set, Draper looked set to level when he went 5-2 up in the second having secured a double-break.

However, he would fail to take six set points spread across the next three games as Landaluce broke twice to level at 5-5.

Draper saved a match point for Landaluce before bringing up a chance of his own to force a tie break, but he was denied before his opponent closed out the match in just short of two hours.

The 24-year-old appeared extremely glum in the closing stages, but at least appeared to finish the match without any major fitness issues.

During his defeat to Terence Atmane in Montreal, the power of Draper's shots notably dropped off in the third set, while he was also in tears during the changeover.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Draper in tears on return from injury at the Canadian Open.

The circumstances in Montreal suggested Draper had reaggravated the left-arm injury that has plagued him since June 2025, at which point he had reached a career-high world ranking of fourth, but a swift return to the practice courts in Cincinnati calmed concern over his physical state.

While only Draper and his team know his true physical condition, it is clear that he is struggling to find anything like his best form, with the final major of the year - the US Open - starting in New York on August 30.

Norrie fights back to beat Prizmic

Cameron Norrie continued his strong form by coming from behind to beat Croatia's Dino Prizmic.

Norrie lost the first set but showed his trademark grit to come through 3-6 6-1 6-4 in just short of two hours.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Cincinnati Open match between Cameron Norrie vs Dino Prizmic.

After a six-match losing streak that included a first-round exit at Wimbledon, Norrie has found form on the hard courts.

He reached the semi-finals at the Los Cabos Open in Mexico, before following that up with an impressive run to the last eight at the Masters 1000 event in Montreal.

However, he faces a tough task to go any further in Cincinnati, with top seed Alexander Zverev awaiting him in the second round after receiving a bye.
